1s : 9017 ( Pat4 Ill') - ?983

.' EXPLANATORY \ NOTE ' .

>

/

Transportation by rope aerially is another type of transportation system like railways, roads, etc. The passengers are transported by means of a carrier/carriers suspended on tensioned steel wire rope/wire ropes supported at intervals to limit sagging and thereby prevent passengers from touching the ground except at planned points. This is particularly useful in regions where the ability of surmounting natural barriers gives them a great advantage over railways or roads, both of which may need heavy civil engineering work to secure easy gradients. Aerial r.opeways are inexpensive to maintain;- their power demand is modest and they are not seriously affected by adverse climatic conditions. It can negotiate valleys, steep gradients, go in a straight line and is limited only by storm condifions and visibility. The merits of aerial ropeways over other modes of transport have made aerial ropeways the Mining industry has adopted the aerial ropechoice of the mining industry in its daily operations. ways mainly for transporting sand from river banks to pit head for storing purposes. In addition aerial ropeway are also being used for transporting coal from pit headlwasheries to washeries/steel . plants. The expense of underground mine working introduces fatigue and reduces the actual working This problem can be solved by introduction of hours of the workers resulting in.lower efficiency. mechanical means of transport such as manriding haulages, locomotive transport or aerial ropeways. For proper selection and design of the mechan-ical means of transport of men, the first step This part of standard, therefore, aims at listing the data to would be to collect the data required. be supplied to the manufacturers by intending purchaser of an aerial system for transportation of oassenaers in underaround .mines or similar operations.. The other parts-aim at listina the data to by the intending purchasers of following types of aerial system: be supplied to the m%ufacturers Part Part Part Part Part I II IV .V VI Transportation Transportation Transportation Portable Transportation of goods of, passengers, surface of goods, underground of forestry products
